architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the low-drift formulation-level suppression result only if SI_15_60 is below 3.57% in every one of at least two valid independent repeats; this is less than half the frozen 7.13% linear-dilution prediction.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If SI_15_60 is below 3.57% in every valid repeat, H-CORE is falsified at the registered threshold. If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.13% in every valid repeat, H-RESIN is falsified. Any discordant repeats or results from 3.57% through below 7.13% are unresolved by these thresholds. H-DUAL cannot be falsified by this dual-axis card.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: If H-CORE is falsified by SI_15_60 below 3.57%, next run a matched 20 wt% acrylic-only M-HOLD-120 arm to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL. If H-RESIN is falsified by SI_15_60 at or above 7.13%, next run an unmodified E2-core M-HOLD-120 control under matched preparation and thermal history to test whether the inherited E1-based reference is transferable.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Per-repeat SI_15_60 = 100 * (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, measured during the 120 C hold for at least two independent preparations.
judge_normalized.rationale: This card is a defensible mitigation experiment under sparse evidence: it directly tests 120 C hot-hold drift, has a 3.56 percentage-point separation between the frozen H-CORE and strong-suppression thresholds, and uses modifier levels inside the supported intervention region. The result can establish only formulation-level rheological suppression, not a molecular mechanism or tackifier necessity.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Proposer and the Robustness Adjudicator on the preferred card S1C51::M-HOLD-120 because it is in the stable tied top set, directly measures the failure mode, and uses the most directly supported 20 wt% acrylic-like and 5 wt% tackifier-like levels without the larger 22.5-25 wt% perturbation. I accept the Skeptic's and Robustness Adjudicator's objections that the E1-derived benchmark is uncertain, process state is uncontrolled, and H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains entangled. I do not replace the selected card with their requested multi-arm set because the output contract permits one experiment card and no matched-set card is supplied; those controls are therefore assigned as conditional follow-ups rather than silently added to the selected experiment.

planner.failure_mode: Excessive viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 °C (thermal-hold drift).
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run measured SI_15_60 = 0.5154, corresponding to a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 °C; by contrast, E1 increased 9.51% over the same window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only two original formulations, E1 and E5, have local 120 °C hold trajectories, each represented by one four-point run over 15–90 min. No thermal-hold trajectory is available for E2 or for any acrylic-like or tackifier-like candidate, and no independent hold repeats are present. In comparison, temperature response is measured at six temperatures from 80 to 130 °C for multiple runs, and realized viscosity-level variability is directly documented for E2 despite its large spread.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min during a 120 °C hold and report the directly observed SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15.
Use at least two independent preparations per tested composition so that differences near the declared 2 percentage-point hold-drift resolution are interpretable.

Include compositions that permit separation of acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like effects: at minimum an acrylic-only arm and a composition with the acrylic-like axis plus a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction, referenced to the same E2 reactive-core anchor.

Compute the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction from E1 drift and each candidate's reactive mass fraction before observing results; compare measured drift with that frozen prediction and with the H-RESIN threshold of less than half the linear prediction.
Record preparation and thermal histories so that realized-state displacement is not silently attributed to formulation chemistry.
Measure a fresh-sample viscosity anchor within the locally supported temperature range, preferably at 110 °C, to locate each realization's viscosity level independently of its hold drift.

If temperature-response transferability is part of candidate interpretation, verify the anchor-based 120 and 130 °C predictions by direct measurements rather than extrapolating beyond the measured 80–130 °C range.
planner.scientific_question: At matched 120 °C residence time, does resin modification of the E2-anchored reactive core reduce SI_15_60 only in proportion to reactive-mass dilution, suppress it substantially beyond that prediction, or require a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction in addition to the acrylic-like modifier to reach the low-drift regime?

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.57% across at least two repeats, drift is less than half the frozen 7.13% linear-dilution prediction. This falsifies H-CORE at the registered separation scale and supports superlinear resin suppression. Because both modifier axes are active, the result remains equally compatible with H-RESIN and H-DUAL and cannot establish that the tackifier is required.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.13%, H-RESIN is falsified and the low-drift predictions of the resin-suppression alternatives are not observed. Agreement near 7.13% supports H-CORE's linear-dilution rule; a value materially above it would establish failure of superlinear suppression but would not, by itself, confirm H-CORE. H-DUAL is not formally falsified under its registered acrylic-only falsification rule.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.57% and 7.13% indicates partial or unresolved suppression: it does not meet the strong H-RESIN acceptance threshold and does not meet its linear-or-higher falsification threshold. If it is more than the 2 percentage-point resolution below 7.13%, H-CORE is disfavored or falsified while the magnitude of superlinear suppression remains insufficiently strong; H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold across at least two independent repeats

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has identical deterministic VOI and lower total modifier burden, but its 15% acrylic level is supported only as a directional lower-region point with an unverified literature denominator, whereas 20% is directly commensurate with repeated external examples.
It has identical deterministic VOI and lies inside the supported region, but 17.5% acrylic is an interpolated design level rather than the directly evidenced approximately 19-20% cluster.

It has identical deterministic VOI and remains inside the supported region, but 22.5% acrylic is a larger perturbation than needed and is less directly anchored than the approximately 19-20% evidence cluster.

It has identical deterministic VOI and 25% acrylic has direct analogue support, but it imposes the largest modifier burden and greatest departure from the characterized E2 reactive core among the tied cards.

proposer.reasoning: The matched-window 120 C hold directly measures the least-resolved and decision-critical isothermal drift coordinate without regression, extrapolation, or imputation. S1C51 separates two of the three registered hypothesis pairs by contrasting the 7.13% H-CORE prediction with the 3.57% low-drift prediction shared by H-RESIN and H-DUAL. Its 20% acrylic and 5% tackifier levels are both in strongly supported external intervention regions. The experiment cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict low drift when both modifier axes are active; an acrylic-only hold would be required for that distinction. Process-state risk remains moderate, so preparation and thermal histories must be recorded and at least two independent repeats used.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C51 uses 20% acrylic-like modifier, matching the strongest directly commensurate external evidence cluster at approximately 19-20%, together with 5% minor tackifier-like modifier in the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% region. It therefore remains fully inside both supported intervention regions without relying on the provisionally noncommensurate 15% acrylic evidence or imposing the larger perturbation represented by 22.5-25% acrylic.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Retain S1C51::M-HOLD-120 as the focal dual-axis arm, but replace the stand-alone experiment with a matched controlled set that includes, at minimum, an unmodified E2-core hold and a 20 wt% acrylic-only hold; a tackifier-only arm is also preferred. Use the same controlled preparation and thermal history, at least three independent preparations per composition, a prespecified rule for discordant repeats and uncertainty propagation, and verified modifier reactive functionality before calculating reactive mass fraction or NCO:OH.
residual_decision_risk: The single-run E1 reference remains uncertain and differs from the E2-derived core in labeled NCO:OH.
M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state, and six process fields are missing; unmatched realization history could be attributed incorrectly to formulation chemistry.
Without the acrylic-only companion arm, H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain unresolved; without a tackifier-only arm, individual-axis and interaction effects remain incompletely attributed.
No prespecified rule is supplied for discordant repeats, failed runs, averaging, or propagation of reference uncertainty.
Modifier reactive functionality is unverified, so the assumed reactive mass fraction and inherited NCO:OH basis may be invalid.
Bulk viscosity drift can support formulation-level rheological suppression but cannot establish the stated molecular encounter or non-reactive-continuum mechanism.
The exact candidate grid and refinement algorithm were formalized retrospectively and lack a contemporaneous repository-freeze artifact.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The proposed stand-alone S1C51 hold does not cleanly identify suppression relative to its own reactive core because its 7.13% H-CORE benchmark is inherited from a single E1 hold at NCO:OH = 1.7, whereas S1C51 preserves the E2-derived NCO:OH = 1.8 core. A concurrent unmodified E2-core hold under matched preparation and thermal history is therefore needed to separate reference uncertainty and core differences from modifier effects. In addition, every experiment in the tied top set activates both modifier axes and leaves H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled; adding the 20 wt% acrylic-only hold supplies discrimination that the tied set does not encode. The direct SI_15_60 measurement remains appropriate, but S1C51 should not be run or interpreted as an isolated arm.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The tied top set remained unchanged in all 25 tested one-term perturbation scenarios: each weight was scaled from 0.5 to 1.5, top_experiment_set_stability was 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary reports survival across the entire sweep. Thus no tested perturbation would remove S1C51::M-HOLD-120 from the tied top set, and there is no decision-changing tested weighting to assess as scientifically defensible. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is only 0.004583, and joint perturbations or scalings outside the tested range were not evaluated.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 directly measures values capable of meeting the stated H-RESIN falsification threshold of SI_15_60 at or above 7.13% and the stated strong H-CORE rejection threshold below 3.57%. The 3.56-point gap between those predictions exceeds the declared 2.00-point resolution. Practical adjudication is incomplete because no rule is specified for discordant repeats or propagated uncertainty from the single-run E1 reference. H-DUAL is not falsifiable with this dual-axis arm, which the Proposer explicitly acknowledges.
leakage_findings: No direct reliance on the withheld target hold outcome is visible in the supplied trace.

The current exact v2 grid and fine-refinement algorithm were formalized after the validation experiment, and no repository freeze artifact is available; although the payload states that validation coordinates and outcomes were excluded, the exact retrospective candidate-space implementation is not independently auditable as a contemporaneous prospective freeze.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A deviation from 7.13% could be called falsification of H-CORE even though it may reflect uncertainty in the single-run E1 baseline or the E1-to-E2 core difference rather than superlinear modifier suppression.
objections.objection: The nominal H-CORE prediction for S1C51 is 7.13% and the shared H-RESIN/H-DUAL low-drift prediction is 3.57%, a 3.56 percentage-point separation that exceeds the declared 2.00-point resolution. Thus the claimed numerical separation is not below resolution. However, the 7.13% reference is derived from E1_drift = 9.51%, which comes from only one E1 hold run, and the protocol propagates no uncertainty from that reference. E1 also has NCO:OH = 1.7, whereas the candidate preserves the E2 core labeled NCO:OH = 1.8. Without a concurrent unmodified E2-core hold, the experiment tests a frozen E1-based rule rather than cleanly establishing that drift is controlled by the S1C51 reactive core and stoichiometry alone.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could support only the phenomenological claim that this dual-axis composition has lower-than-linear drift. It could not support acrylic-specific suppression, tackifier-required suppression, modifier specialization, or a causal interaction assignment.
objections.objection: S1C51 activates both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 20.0 wt% and TK100 is 5.0 wt%, while the reactive mass fraction falls to 0.7500. Consequently, a low SI_15_60 cannot be attributed to the acrylic-like modifier, the minor tackifier-like modifier, their interaction, or tackifier necessity. In addition, M-HOLD-120 has controls_process_state = false and process_state_risk_detail reports six missing process fields with score 0.75; recording histories does not itself impose a matched process state or provide a concurrent control.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: None for the directness of SI_15_60 itself; uncertainty and process-state concerns remain separate from observable interpretation.
objections.objection: No material interpretability defect is present in the primary observable. SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is calculated directly from the measured 15- and 60-minute viscosities at 120 C; it requires no regression, extrapolation, shared-shape model, or imputation. The 30- and 45-minute observations are supplementary rather than necessary to derive the registered primary endpoint.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Borderline or discordant repeat results could be classified post hoc, and no result from S1C51 alone could formally falsify the tackifier-required hypothesis.
objections.objection: The numerical criteria are physically attainable by the specified measurement: SI_15_60 can be observed below 3.57% or at/above 7.13%. Nevertheless, the phrase 'across at least two repeats' lacks a prespecified adjudication rule for discordant repeats, averaging, confidence intervals, or failed runs. The protocol also cannot meet H-DUAL's registered falsification criterion, which requires an acrylic-only composition to reach low drift, because S1C51 contains 5.0 wt% tackifier. The Proposer correctly admits this H-DUAL limitation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low drift result could be overstated as evidence for a specific molecular or mesoscale suppression mechanism when it establishes only formulation-level superlinear rheological suppression.
objections.objection: No direct use of the withheld S1C51 hold outcome is shown. However, the mechanistic wording of H-RESIN—suppression by 'lowering the effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species within a non-reactive continuum'—cannot be established by SI_15_60 alone. The protocol measures bulk viscosity drift and includes no chemical-conversion, functional-group, phase-morphology, or molecular-encounter measurement. The assumption that the modifiers form a non-reactive continuum is also not secured by the protocol; the supplied E2 stoichiometry note explicitly requires recalculation if a modifier has reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a matched set under the same controlled preparation and thermal history: an unmodified E2-core control, a 20 wt% acrylic-only arm, a tackifier-only arm, and the 20 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% tackifier dual-axis arm, with at least three independent preparations per composition. Prespecify whether decisions use each repeat, the mean, or a confidence interval; propagate uncertainty in the reference drift; and verify modifier reactive functionality so the reactive mass fraction and NCO:OH basis are valid. At minimum, add the unmodified E2-core and acrylic-only holds to the proposed S1C51 hold.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The claimed H-CORE versus suppression discrimination depends on an exact 7.13% linear-dilution benchmark inherited from a single E1 hold run on an NCO:OH = 1.7 formulation, while S1C51 uses the E2-derived NCO:OH = 1.8 core and no concurrent unmodified E2-core hold is included. Reference uncertainty and the core change are therefore not separated from the modifier effect.

tool_trace.reason: This must be obtained first to load the upstream state-aware material structure, shared thermal-response evidence, state-calibration implications, and E1/E5 drift contrast before any candidate or experiment ranking.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
